svg.title: A 5-year-old boy had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that lasted 12 minutes. He was given IV lorazepam and the jerking stopped about 2 minutes later. Ten minutes after the dose he is hard to rouse, his breathing is noisy and snoring at 22/min, SpO2 is 93% on room air, and his heart rate is 108/min.
svg.desc: Effectiveness of a benzodiazepine is judged by whether the seizure stopped, and it did, within 2 minutes. Being hard to rouse and confused is the expected postictal state, which can last from 30 minutes to several hours, so it does not mean the drug failed. A heart rate of 108/min is within range for a 5-year-old and says nothing about seizure control. Snoring respirations with a saturation of 93% mean the tongue and secretions are partly blocking the airway, and side-lying positioning opens it and lowers aspiration risk. Forcing in an oral airway is not done, and waiting on an EEG delays care the child needs right now.
